title: One-step CRISPR-Cas9 protocol for conditional knockouts in Drosophila melanogaster

The parent repair plasmid, pTVGFP was derived from TVΔattP-Pax-Cherry, where the pax-Cherry marker is replaced with pax-GFP (Poernbacher et al., 2019, Yu et al., 2020). The pax-GFP marker allows selection based on GFP signal in the larval CNS, as well as the adult eye and ocelli (Horn et al., 2000). The boundaries of the 5′ and 3′ homology arms should be no more than 50bp away from the double strand break, ideally less than 10bp away if possible. Crucially, in order to prevent Cas9 from cleaving the repair plasmid before it has a chance to integrate, the homology arms MUST NOT contain the full target site. The homology arms may contain part of the target site but MUST NOT include the PAM sequence (nGG). Alternatively, a few bases in the 10 nucleotides proceeding the PAM and the PAM itself can be changed in the target site sequence in the repair plasmid (as in the example of DWnt4[cKO]). The safest strategy is to include no more than the first 5–10bp of the target site in your homology arm.7.Design primers for insertion of the 3′ homology arm into the pTVGFP repair vector via multiple cloning site 2 (MCS2) using T4 ligation (NEB):a.Identify ∼1000bp downstream of CRISPR-Cas9 target site number 2 (starting from the middle of the site. Alternatively, choose new CRISPR target sites.

steps.title: Identify target regions
steps.instruction: Obtain the full genomic sequence of the gene of interest from FlyBase, label all coding exons and UTRs, and view the sequence in the UCSC Genome Browser. Highlight a non‑conserved region ~500 bp upstream of the 5′UTR (or desired 5′ cut site) and a second non‑conserved region ~500 bp downstream of the 1st exon (or desired 3′ cut site). Ensure the chosen regions do not contain conserved regulatory elements, FRT, attP or loxP sites.

steps.title: Select sgRNA target sites
steps.instruction: Copy each highlighted region into the Drosophila melanogaster CRISPR target finder (http://targetfinder.flycrispr.neuro.brown.edu/), set guide length to 20 nt, select “High Stringency” and “NGG only” PAM. Choose sgRNAs with no predicted off‑target sites; if unavoidable, pick sgRNAs whose off‑targets lie on a different chromosome.

steps.title: Verify sgRNA sites in host DNA
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from ~5 individuals of the Cas9‑expressing strain (e.g., yw;;nos‑Cas9(III‑attP2)) by chilling flies at 4 °C for 5 min, crushing in 50 µL squishing buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.2, 1 mM EDTA, 25 mM NaCl, add Proteinase K 200 µg/mL just before use), and following the Single‑fly DNA prep protocol. If yield/purity is low, use the ChargeSwitch gDNA Micro Tissue Kit (half the recommended buffer volumes). PCR‑amplify ~150 bp flanking each sgRNA site using a 50 µL Q5 2× Master Mix reaction (25 µL 2× Master Mix, 2.5 µL forward primer 10 µM, 2.5 µL reverse primer 10 µM, 2 µL gDNA, water to 50 µL). Cycle: 98 °C 30 s; 35‑40 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, annealing 58‑67 °C 30 s (determine Tm with NEB Tm calculator), 72 °C 30 s/kb; final extension 72 °C 2 min; hold 4‑10 °C. Run products on a 1 % agarose gel, gel‑purify with QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit, and send for Sanger sequencing. If SNPs are found in any target site, return to step 2 and select alternative sgRNAs.

steps.title: Design sgRNA cloning primers
steps.instruction: Design primers for cloning each protospacer into pCFD4 according to Port et al., 2014. If the protospacer starts with G, use the 19‑nt sequence (N = 19). If it does not start with G, either prepend a G (making G+19 nt) or use the full 20 nt sequence. Record the primer sequences for later PCR.

steps.title: Prepare Ampicillin LB plates
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L LB broth: 5 g yeast extract, 10 g tryptone, 10 g NaCl, 15 g agar. Autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min. Cool to 55 °C and add Ampicillin to a final concentration of 100 µg/mL. Pour into petri dishes and let solidify. Store plates at 4 °C for up to 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare squishing buffer
steps.instruction: Mix the following per litre: 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.2, 1 mM EDTA, 25 mM NaCl. Add Proteinase K to 200 µg/mL immediately before use. Store at room temperature for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Clone sgRNAs into pCFD4
steps.instruction: Amplify pCFD4 with the sgRNA cloning primers using Q5 2× Master Mix (same mix as step 3) and an annealing temperature of 61 °C. Digest the PCR product and 2 µg pCFD4 vector with BbsI‑HF at 37 °C for 1 h in 10 µL (1 µL 10× CutSmart buffer, 0.5 µL BbsI‑HF, water to 10 µL). Run both digested vector (6.4 kb) and PCR product (~600 bp) on a 1 % agarose gel, excise bands and gel‑purify with QIAquick Kit. Assemble insert and vector with NEB Gibson Assembly Master Mix according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Transform DH5α competent cells, plate on Ampicillin LB plates (100 µg/mL). Incubate overnight at 37 °C, pick several colonies, inoculate 5 mL LB + Ampicillin and grow 16 h, then perform a Qiagen MiniPrep. Verify insertion by Sanger sequencing using primer GACACAGCGCGTACGTCCTTCG. Prepare a Maxiprep of the confirmed pCFD4 plasmid (Invitrogen PureLink HiPure Plasmid Maxiprep Kit) and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Design repair plasmid primers
steps.instruction: From the genomic DNA of the Cas9 line, design ~1000 bp 5′ and 3′ homology arms flanking each cut site, ensuring the arms lie ≤50 bp (ideally ≤10 bp) from the double‑strand break and do NOT contain the full protospacer plus PAM. Include only the first 5‑10 bp of the target site if needed. Design primers that add the appropriate restriction sites for MCS1 (5′ arm) and MCS2 (3′ arm) and, for the 5′ arm, append a segment homologous to the linearized vector for Gibson assembly. Also design primers that embed the FRT71 cassette (GAAGTTCCTATTCCGAAGTTCCTATTCTCTAGAAAGTATAGGAACTTC) within the forward and reverse primers for the region between the two cut sites.

steps.title: Clone 3′ homology arm
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the 3′ homology arm using the primers from step 7 (Q5 mix as in step 3). Gel‑purify the product. Digest 2 µg pTVGFP backbone with the two restriction enzymes selected for MCS2 (see step 7) in 10 µL (1 µL 10× CutSmart, 0.5 µL each enzyme, water to 10 µL) at the enzymes’ recommended temperature (use NEB Double Digest Finder for buffer). Digest the PCR product similarly (34 µL PCR product, 4 µL 10× CutSmart, 1 µL each enzyme, water to 10 µL). Ligate backbone and insert with T4 DNA Ligase (NEB) following the manufacturer’s protocol. Transform DH5α, plate on Ampicillin LB plates, incubate overnight. Pick colonies, culture 16 h, perform MiniPrep, and verify insertion by sequencing with primers GTTGTGGTTTGTCCAAACTCAT (forward) and CCATGATTACGCCAAGC (reverse).

steps.title: Clone 5′ arm and FRT cassette
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the 5′ homology arm and the FRT‑flanked region using primers from step 7 (same Q5 mix). Gel‑purify both products. Digest the pTVGFP‑3′arm plasmid (obtained in step 8) with the two restriction enzymes selected for MCS1 (see step 7) using the same digestion conditions as above. Assemble the digested backbone with the 5′ arm and FRT cassette by Gibson Assembly (NEB) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Transform DH5α, plate on Ampicillin LB, incubate overnight. Pick colonies, culture 16 h, MiniPrep, and verify insertion by sequencing with primers CAGTCACGACGTTGTAAAACGA (5′ arm forward) and GAATTAGCTCTAATTGAATTAGTCTCTAATTGAATT (pTVGFP Pax reverse).

steps.title: Purify final repair plasmid
steps.instruction: Perform a Maxiprep of the verified pTVFRT‑GFP donor plasmid using the Invitrogen PureLink HiPure Plasmid Maxiprep Kit. Store the purified plasmid at –20 °C until injection.

steps.title: Prepare injection mix
steps.instruction: Expand the chosen Cas9‑expressing strain (e.g., yw;;nos‑Cas9(III‑attP2)). In ddH₂O, mix pCFD4 at 100 ng/µL and pTVFRT‑GFP at 500 ng/µL. For a typical injection of 300–400 embryos, use 300 µg of pCFD4 and 500 µg of pTVFRT‑GFP (final volume ≈ 3 mL). The injection volume should be <5 % of the egg volume.

steps.title: Inject embryos
steps.instruction: Co‑inject the plasmid mix into pre‑cellularized embryos of the Cas9 line. If no in‑house microinjection facility is available, send the mix to a commercial injection service (they typically inject 200–300 embryos per batch).

steps.title: Cross and screen progeny
steps.instruction: Raise injected embryos to adulthood, cross each G₀ adult to w1118 flies. Screen the G₁ progeny for GFP fluorescence in the larval central nervous system or adult eyes/ocelli using a fluorescence stereomicroscope.

steps.title: Establish balanced lines
steps.instruction: Select individual GFP‑positive transformants, establish balanced stocks (e.g., using appropriate balancer chromosomes), and maintain the lines.

steps.title: Validate insertion by PCR
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from each transformant line (use the single‑fly squishing protocol). Design two primer pairs: (i) one forward primer just outside the 5′ homology arm and one reverse primer within the GFP coding sequence; (ii) one forward primer within GFP and one reverse primer just outside the 3′ homology arm. Perform PCR using the Q5 2× Master Mix and cycling conditions described in step 3. Verify the expected product sizes by agarose gel electrophoresis and, if desired, sequence the amplicons.

steps.title: Optional Cre‑mediated excision
steps.instruction: If removal of the pax‑GFP cassette is desired, cross the balanced line to a Cre recombinase line (e.g., Bloomington #766 or #851). Select progeny that have lost GFP fluorescence, confirming excision by PCR.

steps.title: Optional attP reintegration
steps.instruction: To introduce additional sequences (e.g., GAL4, HA‑tagged CDS) at the attP landing site, prepare a PhiC31‑mediated integration vector and inject it into embryos carrying the attP site following standard PhiC31 protocols (see Hoppe and Ashe, 2021). Screen for successful integration by PCR or fluorescence as appropriate.
